result.title: Exploring the Privacy--Size Tradeoff for Differentially Private Self-Attentive Variational Autoencoders
result.comment: ICAIF 2026, Financial AI Security, Privacy and Safety workshop. Poster session
result.summary: Data tends to be most useful when it is shared, and the data most worth sharing is often the data that privacy obligations restrict. Synthetic data from a generator trained under differential privacy (DP) is one way to reconcile the two, but its utility depends on the privacy budget $\varepsilon$ and on how much data the generator sees - a parameter that most data sharing applications of synthetic data control. We present SAVANT, a self-attentive variational autoencoder for tabular data trained with DP-SGD that, to our knowledge, is the first to combine attention, a VAE, and DP in one tabular model. We evaluate it against two marginal mechanisms, PrivBayes and MST, jointly over the privacy budget and the dataset size on two public datasets, measuring the utility a downstream classifier loses by training on synthetic rather than real data. We find that, under the same DP guarantee, more data generally means more utility. For the marginal mechanisms it absorbs most of what a strict budget costs, and a noise-scaling argument suggests DP-SGD exchanges data fo budget at a worse rate. Two independent membership-inference attacks, judged against a measured null, found no aggregate membership signal.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 SAVANT——一个在 DP-SGD 下训练的表格数据自注意力 VAE 生成器，在两个公开数据集上联合考察隐私预算与数据规模对下游分类效用的影响，并用两种成员推断攻击检验隐私泄漏。
AI.relevance_reason: 研究主题是表格合成数据的差分隐私与规模权衡，与视觉/多模态推理中的内部表征、证据使用或停止决策没有实质联系；注意力与 VAE 在此仅作为表格生成器结构，未涉及推理期状态生成或视觉信息保留，故不入选。
